line: A leading private bank with a large financial-services group

brief.t: A leading private bank with 2,276 branches (March 2026) and about 5.1 crore customers (September 2026).
MD & CEO Ashok Vaswani (since Jan 2024) steps down on 31 Dec 2026; RBI has approved Anup Kumar Saha as the next MD & CEO from 1 Jan 2027.
FY 2025-26 standalone net profit was ₹14,008 crore, up 2% on a like-for-like basis.
Q2 FY27 (Jul–Sep 2026) profit rose 29% to ₹4,212 crore; Gross NPA improved to 1.04%.
One of the best-capitalised banks: capital adequacy of 21.9% in September 2026.

timeline.t: Uday Kotak started Kotak Mahindra Finance as a finance company.
Became a bank: the first Indian finance company (NBFC) to get a banking licence.
Ashok Vaswani became MD & CEO after founder Uday Kotak stepped down; C S Rajan became Part-time Chairman.
RBI approved Anup Kumar Saha as the next MD & CEO, from 1 Jan 2027.

model.how: Kotak earns mainly from the gap between interest on loans and interest paid to depositors, plus fees. Its group companies in broking, car finance, life insurance and asset management add a large share of group profit.
flow: Bank lends to people and businesses

points: RBI must approve a private bank's CEO. That's why Kotak's next CEO needed RBI clearance in 2026.
Kotak competes with HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and Axis Bank, and is known for a high CASA ratio and strong capital.
Big theme for interviews: banks are investing heavily in technology and AI.

points.t: Standalone net profit ₹4,212 cr, up 29%; group profit ₹5,645 cr, up 26%.

numbers.say: Kotak's profit rose 29% last quarter, its bad loans are just about 1%, and it is preparing for a change of CEO in January 2027.

rivals.note: Kotak is smaller than HDFC, ICICI and Axis by profit, but has one of the highest capital ratios.

network.local: Kotak opens fewer branches than its big rivals and spends more on technology, so many roles focus on digital and relationship banking.

employer.note: From the FY 2025-26 annual report. Hiring focused on technology roles, and attrition improved from 33.3% a year earlier.

csr.t: Kotak's CSR work is run mainly through the Kotak Education Foundation and focuses on education, livelihoods and healthcare.

frameworks.note: Framework views are analysis built from the verified facts on this page, not company statements.

glossary.Net profit: What is left after all costs, provisions and taxes. The bank's final earnings.
glossary.Net Interest Income: Interest earned on loans minus interest paid on deposits. A bank's main earning.
glossary.Net interest margin: Net Interest Income as a % of the bank's interest-earning assets. Shows how profitable lending is.
glossary.Gross NPA: Non-Performing Asset: a loan not repaid for 90+ days. Gross NPA is the % of all loans that have gone bad.
glossary.Net NPA: Bad loans after subtracting the money already set aside (provisions) for them. Lower is better.
glossary.CASA ratio: Share of deposits in Current and Savings accounts. These pay little interest, so a higher CASA means cheaper funds.
glossary.Capital adequacy ratio: The bank's own capital compared with the risk in its loans. RBI requires a minimum; higher means safer.
glossary.Provisions: Money set aside from profit to cover loans that may not be repaid.
glossary.Deposits: Money customers keep with the bank in savings, current and fixed deposit accounts.
glossary.Advances: Loans given by the bank to customers and businesses.
glossary.Dividend: Part of the profit paid to shareholders, per share.
glossary.Treasury gains: Profit from buying and selling bonds and other investments. It can swing a lot each quarter.
glossary.Attrition: The % of employees who leave in a year. Also called employee turnover.
glossary.RBI: Reserve Bank of India, which regulates all banks in India.
glossary.KYC: Know Your Customer: checking a customer's identity before opening an account.
glossary.MSME: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises: small businesses that banks lend to.
glossary.Cross-sell: Selling an extra product (like a credit card) to an existing customer.
glossary.Public sector bank: A bank where the Government of India owns the majority of shares.
glossary.BRSR: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report: an official yearly report on people, environment and governance that big listed companies must publish.

Role knowledge, the bank and HR questions

Finance.q: Why is Kotak's capital adequacy so high, and why does it matter?
Finance.a: It holds a lot of surplus capital (21.9% in Sep 2026), which protects against losses and lets it grow or acquire without raising money.

Finance.q: Profit rose 29% but margin fell. How?
Finance.a: Interest income grew 16% and provisions were lower, even though the margin dropped to 4.31%.

Finance.q: What is CASA, and what is Kotak's?
Finance.a: Current and savings account deposits as a share of total deposits; cheap funds for the bank. Kotak's was 43.3% in March 2026.

Marketing.q: How would you market Kotak's app-based savings account to college students?
Marketing.a: Instant digital onboarding, campus ambassadors, UPI rewards and simple money-management features.

Marketing.q: Kotak has fewer branches than rivals. How would you win customers in a new city?
Marketing.a: Digital-first campaigns, partnerships with employers for salary accounts, and a few well-placed branches.

HR.q: Kotak's attrition is about 32.5%. How would you reduce it?
HR.a: Better onboarding, internal job moves (Kotak recorded 6,500 in FY26), clear growth paths and manager training.

HR.q: How would you manage a CEO transition for employees?
HR.a: Clear communication, continuity of goals, and visible leadership connect sessions.

Sales.q: Sell me a Kotak 811 savings account.
Sales.a: Ask about needs, then link instant digital opening, app features and offers. Close with a clear next step.

Operations.q: How can technology reduce errors in account opening?
Operations.a: Digital KYC, automated checks and tracking turnaround time at each step.

Other.q: What do you know about Kotak Mahindra Bank?
Other.a: A leading private bank: ₹14,008 cr profit in FY26, very strong capital, and a new CEO, Anup Kumar Saha, from Jan 2027.

interview.why_us: Kotak combines strong discipline with ambition: profit rose 29% last quarter, bad loans are about 1%, and it holds some of the strongest capital in Indian banking. With a new CEO from January 2027 and a big push on technology, it is entering a new phase. I want to be part of that and contribute to [your role] from day one.

gd.t: Should banks hold more capital than required?
gd.for: Kotak's 21.9% capital makes it very safe.
gd.against: Unused capital can lower returns for shareholders.

gd.for: Kotak grew with fewer branches and more tech spending.
gd.against: Rivals use large branch networks to reach small towns.
